stem: The graph shows Class A and Class B student counts for Monday and Tuesday as adjacent bars on a common scale.

parts.text: Which claim correctly reads the graph?

options.text: Call the display a double column graph only, with no comparison of bar heights.
On Monday, Class A has $18$ students and Class B has $12$; on Tuesday, Class A has $22$ and Class B has $16$, read from adjacent bars on one scale.
Drawing adjacent bars is what creates the Monday and Tuesday categories.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A clustered column graph places related bars side by side under each day so heights on the shared scale can be compared.

teacher.key_rationale: Clustered columns put Class A and Class B bars adjacent under each day on one scale; reading those heights compares the datasets. Naming the graph type alone substitutes a label. Saying the bars create the days reverses the encoding.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote single bar chart as a clustered column graph for Mon/Tue with Class A (shaded) and Class B (open) adjacent bars.
